claims.head: The Sharks’ edge in shots from defensemen
claims.body: The Sharks are near the top of the league for shots from defensemen, and the Canucks are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 33% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 9th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Max Sasson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 34% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, up from 4% last season.

stakes: The Canucks go in eighth in the Pacific with 7 points, 6 points behind the Sharks, fourth.

SJS.head: The Sharks have a lot going for them
SJS.body: San Jose has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Canucks’ way back in is getting good looks.

VAN.head: A tough matchup for the Canucks
VAN.body: San Jose has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Canucks can pull it off if they get good looks.

items.text: The Sharks are newly without Igor Chernyshov, and have been without Alexander Wennberg since Oct 19.
Macklin Celebrini has a point in five straight games against Vancouver, and 13 points in his last seven against them.
The Canucks have been without Thatcher Demko all season. Leevi Meriläinen is expected to start.
Mason Marchment is two goals from 100.
